creators.name: Joseph Beuys
creators.bio: German artist (1921–1986) who extended sculpture to teaching, discussion and political organising under the name social sculpture. He co-founded the Free International University and was an early figure of the German Greens.
creators.why: He framed society itself as a sculpture everyone shapes, and built works such as 7000 Eichen whose form depended on public funding and collective planting.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、教师与政治行动者
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家（1921–1986），以“社会雕塑”之名把雕塑扩展到教学、讨论与政治组织。他参与创立自由国际大学，也是德国绿党的早期人物。
creators.why_zh: 他把社会本身视为人人参与塑造的雕塑，《7000棵橡树》这样的作品，其形态取决于公众出资和集体种植。

creators.name: Francis Alÿs
creators.bio: Belgian-born artist who has lived in Mexico City since 1986. He works through walks, actions and films, often staged with volunteers, soldiers, children or city workers.
creators.why: Many of his actions are one simple rule handed to a crowd (shovel the dune, fall into step, push the rubbish), and the film records what the crowd makes of it.
creators.bio_zh: 出生于比利时，1986 年起定居墨西哥城。他以行走、行动和影像创作，常与志愿者、士兵、儿童或城市工人一同完成。
creators.why_zh: 他的许多行动只是交给一群人的一条简单规则（铲沙丘、并步齐行、推垃圾），影片记录人群如何把规则变成事件。

creators.name: Marina Abramović
creators.bio: Serbian-born performance artist working since the early 1970s with endurance, the body and the relation between performer and audience.
creators.why: In Rhythm 0 and The Artist Is Present she set strict rules for the audience and left the outcome to what they chose to do.
creators.bio_zh: 出生于塞尔维亚的行为艺术家，自 1970 年代初起以耐力、身体以及表演者与观众的关系为创作核心。
creators.why_zh: 在《节奏 0》和《艺术家在场》中，她为观众设定严格的规则，把结果交给观众自己的选择。

creators.name: Tino Sehgal
creators.bio: British-German artist who makes 'constructed situations': works enacted by trained interpreters in conversation or movement with visitors, with no objects and no photographic documentation.
creators.why: His works exist only as rules passed on orally to interpreters and buyers, and are sold by spoken contract before a notary.
creators.bio_zh: 英德籍艺术家，创作“建构情境”：由受过训练的诠释者与观众交谈或共同行动来完成的作品，没有实物，也不允许拍照记录。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品只以口头传给诠释者和买家的规则存在，并在公证人面前以口头合同出售。

creators.name: Mierle Laderman Ukeles
creators.role: Artist; artist-in-residence of the New York City Department of Sanitation
creators.bio: American artist who wrote the Manifesto for Maintenance Art in 1969 and has been the unsalaried artist-in-residence of New York's Department of Sanitation since 1977.
creators.why: She turned other people's daily maintenance work into art by rule: a declared hour, a handshake, a ritual repeated with thousands of workers.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；纽约市环卫局驻局艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，1969 年写下《维护艺术宣言》，自 1977 年起担任纽约市环卫局的无薪驻局艺术家。
creators.why_zh: 她用规则把他人日常的维护劳动变成艺术：一个被宣告的小时、一次握手、与数千名工人重复的仪式。

creators.name: Tania Bruguera
creators.bio: Cuban artist whose 'behaviour art' (arte de conducta) and 'useful art' (arte útil) place audiences in political situations and build lasting social institutions.
creators.why: Her works hand the microphone, the crowd or the community centre to the public and let their actions become the piece.
creators.bio_zh: 古巴艺术家，她的“行为艺术”（arte de conducta）与“有用的艺术”（arte útil）把观众置于政治情境之中，并建立持续运作的社会机构。
creators.why_zh: 她把麦克风、人群或社区中心交给公众，让公众的行动成为作品。

creators.name: Ai Weiwei
creators.bio: Chinese artist working across installation, architecture, film and social media, known for large participatory projects and for his critique of state power.
creators.why: Fairytale used an open call on his blog to bring 1,001 Chinese citizens to documenta 12, making their journey the work.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、建筑师与社会行动者
creators.bio_zh: 中国艺术家，创作涵盖装置、建筑、电影与社交媒体，以大型参与式项目和对国家权力的批评著称。
creators.why_zh: 《童话》通过他博客上的公开征集，把 1001 名中国公民带到第十二届卡塞尔文献展，他们的旅程就是作品。

creators.name: Jeremy Deller
creators.bio: British artist and Turner Prize winner (2004) who makes processions, re-enactments and public events with large casts of non-professionals.
creators.why: He designs the frame (a re-enactment, a card, a silence) and lets hundreds of volunteers carry it into public space.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，2004 年特纳奖得主，以大量非专业参与者组织游行、历史重演和公共事件。
creators.why_zh: 他设计框架（一场重演、一张卡片、一种沉默），再让数百名志愿者把它带进公共空间。

creators.name: Gillian Wearing
creators.bio: British artist and Turner Prize winner (1997) working with photography and video on confession, identity and the gap between public and private selves.
creators.why: Her Signs series handed the caption to the people in the picture: a single instruction to strangers produced hundreds of self-authored portraits.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，1997 年特纳奖得主，以摄影和影像探讨告白、身份以及公共自我与私人自我之间的落差。
creators.why_zh: 她的《标语》系列把图注交给画面中的人：给陌生人的一条指令，产生了数百张由他们自己署名的肖像。

creators.name: Rirkrit Tiravanija
creators.based: New York, US / Chiang Mai, TH
creators.bio: Thai artist born in Buenos Aires whose installations since the early 1990s turn galleries into kitchens, living rooms and meeting places.
creators.why: His cooking pieces are a standing offer to visitors (free food, a shared table), and the social life that follows is the work.
creators.bio_zh: 生于布宜诺斯艾利斯的泰国艺术家，自 1990 年代初起把画廊变成厨房、客厅和聚会场所。
creators.why_zh: 他的烹饪作品是向观众发出的长期邀请（免费食物、共享餐桌），随之发生的社交生活就是作品。

creators.name: Lygia Clark
creators.bio: Brazilian artist (1920–1988), co-founder of Neo-Concretism, who moved from painting to 'propositions' that participants complete with their own bodies, and later to therapy.
creators.why: She replaced the art object with an instruction or a shared action; the work happens only when others carry it out.
creators.bio_zh: 巴西艺术家（1920–1988），新具体主义的创始人之一，从绘画转向由参与者用身体完成的“提议”，后来转向治疗实践。
creators.why_zh: 她用一条指令或一次共同行动取代艺术品；只有别人去做，作品才会发生。

creators.name: Hélio Oiticica
creators.bio: Brazilian artist (1937–1980) of the Neo-Concrete movement whose Parangolés, Penetrables and Tropicália turned viewers into wearers, dancers and inhabitants.
creators.why: His Parangolé capes exist fully only when someone puts one on and moves; he made them with dancers of the Mangueira samba school.
creators.bio_zh: 巴西艺术家（1937–1980），新具体主义成员，他的《帕兰戈莱》《可穿透物》和《热带主义》把观众变成穿戴者、舞者和居住者。
creators.why_zh: 他的《帕兰戈莱》斗篷只有在有人穿上并舞动时才完整存在；它们是与芒格拉桑巴学校的舞者一起完成的。

creators.name: Guy Debord
creators.role: Writer, filmmaker and founder of the Situationist International
creators.bio: French theorist (1931–1994), founder of the Letterist International and the Situationist International (1957–1972), author of The Society of the Spectacle.
creators.why: He wrote explicit procedures for groups (the dérive) and a rule-based strategy game, treating play and drifting as methods against the spectacle.
creators.role_zh: 作家、电影人、情境主义国际创始人
creators.bio_zh: 法国理论家（1931–1994），字母主义国际与情境主义国际（1957–1972）的创始人，著有《景观社会》。
creators.why_zh: 他为群体写下明确的程序（漂移），也设计了一套规则化的战略游戏，把游戏与漂移当作对抗景观的方法。

creators.name: Suzanne Lacy
creators.bio: American artist who since the 1970s has staged large public performances with communities, often on women, ageing and violence, and who coined the term 'new genre public art'.
creators.why: Her performances give hundreds of participants a score of simple actions and a shared conversation, and broadcast the result.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，自 1970 年代起与社群一起完成大型公共表演，常关注女性、衰老与暴力，并提出“新类型公共艺术”一词。
creators.why_zh: 她的表演给数百名参与者一套简单动作的乐谱和一场共同的对话，再把结果播出。

creators.name: Thomas Hirschhorn
creators.bio: Swiss artist who builds temporary structures from cheap materials, including a series of 'monuments' to philosophers built and run with residents of housing estates.
creators.why: His monuments are built, staffed and used by the local residents under rules he sets: paid work, daily programme, fixed duration.
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，用廉价材料搭建临时结构，其中包括与公共住宅区居民一起建造和运营的一系列哲学家“纪念碑”。
creators.why_zh: 他的纪念碑由当地居民在他设定的规则下建造、值守和使用：有报酬的工作、每日节目、固定期限。

creators.name: Lee Mingwei
creators.bio: Taiwanese-American artist whose participatory installations are built on gifts, meals, letters and conversations between strangers.
creators.why: His works are simple conditions attached to a gift, which visitors carry out of the museum and into the city.
creators.bio_zh: 台裔美国艺术家，他的参与式装置建立在陌生人之间的礼物、饭食、信件和对话之上。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品是附在一份礼物上的简单条件，由观众带出美术馆、带进城市去完成。

creators.name: Collective Actions
creators.bio: Group founded in March 1976 by Andrei Monastyrski, Nikita Alekseev, Georgy Kizevalter and Lev Rubinstein, later joined by Nikolai Panitkov, Elena Elagina, Igor Makarevich, Sergei Romashko and Sabine Hänsgen.
creators.why: Their 'Trips Out of Town' invited a circle of viewers into empty fields where the viewers' waiting, walking and testimony became the action, then documented it in samizdat volumes.
creators.role_zh: 莫斯科观念主义表演团体
creators.bio_zh: 1976 年 3 月由安德烈·莫纳斯蒂尔斯基、尼基塔·阿列克谢耶夫、格奥尔基·基泽瓦尔特和列夫·鲁宾斯坦创立，后来尼古拉·帕尼特科夫、叶莲娜·叶拉金娜、伊戈尔·马卡列维奇、谢尔盖·罗马什科和萨比娜·亨斯根加入。
creators.why_zh: 他们的“出城之旅”邀请一批观众走进空旷的田野，观众的等待、行走和见证就是行动本身，之后再编入地下出版的文集。

creators.name: Hans Haacke
creators.bio: German-born artist who moved from physical and biological systems in the 1960s to 'real-time social systems': polls, visitor profiles and investigations of art-world power.
creators.why: His visitor polls make the museum audience produce the work's data, in public, under a question he sets.
creators.bio_zh: 出生于德国的艺术家，1960 年代从物理与生物系统转向“实时社会系统”：民意调查、观众画像，以及对艺术界权力的调查。
creators.why_zh: 他的观众投票让美术馆观众在他提出的问题下，当众生产作品的数据。

creators.name: Paul Ramírez Jonas
creators.bio: Artist born in California and raised in Honduras whose public works use civic rituals such as keys, oaths and public speech as materials.
creators.why: Key to the City let anyone confer a civic honour on anyone else and turned the key into a pass to a network of sites.
creators.bio_zh: 生于加州、在洪都拉斯长大的艺术家，他的公共作品以钥匙、誓词、公开发言等公民仪式为材料。
creators.why_zh: 《城市之钥》让任何人都能把一项公民荣誉授予任何人，并把钥匙变成通往一组地点的通行证。

creators.name: Tom Marioni
creators.role: Conceptual artist; founder of the Museum of Conceptual Art
creators.bio: American conceptual artist who founded the Museum of Conceptual Art (MOCA) in San Francisco in 1970, which he described as a large-scale social work of art.
creators.why: He declared a recurring social gathering an artwork and has kept it running for decades.
creators.role_zh: 观念艺术家；观念艺术博物馆创始人
creators.bio_zh: 美国观念艺术家，1970 年在旧金山创立观念艺术博物馆（MOCA），并称之为一件大尺度的社会艺术作品。
creators.why_zh: 他把一场定期的社交聚会宣布为艺术作品，并让它持续了几十年。

creators.name: VALIE EXPORT
creators.bio: Austrian artist (1940–2026) and pioneer of feminist performance, Expanded Cinema and video, often working with Peter Weibel in the late 1960s.
creators.why: Tapp und Tastkino offered passers-by one rule-bound act of touch in public, making the audience's choice the content of the 'film'.
creators.bio_zh: 奥地利艺术家（1940–2026），女性主义行为艺术、扩展电影和录像艺术的先驱，1960 年代末常与彼得·魏贝尔合作。
creators.why_zh: 《触摸电影》在公共场合给路人一个受规则约束的触摸行为，观众的选择就是这部“电影”的内容。

creators.name: Improv Everywhere
creators.role: Public performance collective founded by Charlie Todd
creators.bio: New York group founded by Charlie Todd in 2001 that stages unannounced 'missions' in public places with volunteer 'agents' recruited online.
creators.why: Its missions are short written instructions sent to hundreds of volunteers, who carry them out in synchrony among unsuspecting passers-by.
creators.role_zh: 查理·托德创立的公共表演团体
creators.bio_zh: 查理·托德于 2001 年在纽约创立的团体，在公共场所以网上招募的志愿“特工”执行事先不宣布的“任务”。
creators.why_zh: 它的任务是发给数百名志愿者的简短书面指令，他们在不知情的路人中同步执行。

works.title: 7000 Eichen – Stadtverwaldung statt Stadtverwaltung (7000 Oaks)
works.description: For documenta 7 Beuys piled 7,000 basalt steles in front of the Fridericianum in Kassel; each stone left the pile only when an oak was planted with it somewhere in the city.
works.description_zh: 第七届卡塞尔文献展上，博伊斯在弗里德里希阿鲁姆博物馆前堆起 7000 根玄武岩石柱；只有当城市某处种下一棵橡树并配上一根石柱时，石头才会离开石堆。
works.idea_en: A counter you can see: the pile shrinks only as the public plants and pays.
works.idea_zh: 一个看得见的计数器：只有公众种树、出资，石堆才会变小。
works.protocol: Every oak is planted next to one basalt stele taken from the pile on Friedrichsplatz, and a stone may leave the pile only when a tree is planted with it. Each tree-and-stone unit is funded by a sponsor who adopts it (500 Deutsche Mark per unit).
works.protocol_zh: 每棵橡树旁立一根取自弗里德里希广场石堆的玄武岩石柱，只有种下一棵树，才能从石堆中取走一块石头。每组“树加石”由认领它的资助人出资（每组 500 德国马克）。
works.collective: Citizens, schools, companies and donors adopted trees between 1982 and 1987; the 7,000th oak was planted on 12 June 1987 at documenta 8, after Beuys's death, by his son Wenzel next to the first tree. The project cost around three million marks and turned Kassel's streets into a distributed sculpture; Dia Art Foundation later continued it in New York.
works.collective_zh: 1982 至 1987 年间，市民、学校、企业和捐助者认领树木；博伊斯去世后，第 7000 棵橡树于 1987 年 6 月 12 日第八届文献展期间由他的儿子文策尔种在第一棵树旁边。项目总花费约三百万马克，把卡塞尔的街道变成一件分布式雕塑；迪亚艺术基金会后来在纽约延续了这件作品。

works.title: Büro der Organisation für direkte Demokratie durch Volksabstimmung
works.description: At documenta 5 Beuys ran the office of his Organisation for Direct Democracy through Referendum inside the exhibition and talked with visitors about politics every day for the 100 days of the show.
works.description_zh: 第五届卡塞尔文献展期间，博伊斯在展厅里开设“全民公决直接民主组织”的办公室，在展览的 100 天里每天与观众讨论政治。
works.idea_en: An exhibition slot turned into a public office whose content is the visitors' conversation.
works.idea_zh: 把一个展位变成公共办公室，内容就是观众的谈话。
works.protocol: The office is open for the full run of the exhibition (30 June – 8 October 1972); any visitor may enter and debate direct democracy with the artist, who is present every day; the run closes with a staged boxing match 'for direct democracy'.
works.protocol_zh: 办公室在展览全程（1972 年 6 月 30 日至 10 月 8 日）开放；任何观众都可以进来与每天在场的艺术家辩论直接民主；展期以一场“为直接民主而战”的表演性拳击赛结束。
works.collective: Thousands of documenta visitors passed through; a documented day in July 1972 counted 811 visitors, of whom 35 joined the discussion. The work consisted of these exchanges and ended with Beuys's staged boxing match against student Abraham David Christian on 8 October.
works.collective_zh: 数以千计的文献展观众从办公室经过；1972 年 7 月某一天的记录显示有 811 名访客，其中 35 人参与讨论。作品就是这些交流，并以 10 月 8 日博伊斯与学生亚伯拉罕·大卫·克里斯蒂安的表演性拳击赛收尾。

works.title: Cuando la fe mueve montañas (When Faith Moves Mountains)
works.description: On 11 April 2002, 500 volunteers with shovels formed a single line at the foot of a 500-metre sand dune in Ventanilla outside Lima and moved it about 10 centimetres from its original position.
works.description_zh: 2002 年 4 月 11 日，500 名拿着铲子的志愿者在利马郊外文塔尼亚一座长 500 米的沙丘脚下排成一条线，把沙丘从原位推移了约 10 厘米。
works.idea_en: Maximum effort, minimum result: a crowd's coordinated labour as a political image.
works.idea_zh: 最大的努力，最小的结果：人群协调一致的劳动本身就是政治图像。
works.protocol: Volunteers stand shoulder to shoulder in one line along the base of the dune; each shovels sand a short distance forward, the line advances step by step, and the action ends when the whole dune has been displaced by a few centimetres.
works.protocol_zh: 志愿者沿沙丘底部肩并肩排成一条线；每人把沙向前铲一小段，整条线一步步推进，直到整座沙丘被整体挪动几厘米为止。
works.collective: About 500 volunteers, mostly students from Lima, carried out the action in one day, made with Cuauhtémoc Medina and Rafael Ortega; the movement of the dune is invisible, and the work survives as film, photographs and the participants' accounts.
works.collective_zh: 约 500 名志愿者（大多是利马的学生）在一天之内完成了这次行动，合作者为夸乌特莫克·梅迪纳和拉斐尔·奥尔特加；沙丘的位移肉眼看不出，作品以影片、照片和参与者的讲述留存。

works.title: Guards
works.description: Sixty-four Coldstream Guards were dropped off one by one around the City of London and walked until they found each other, gradually assembling into a marching square.
works.description_zh: 64 名冷溪近卫团士兵被逐一放在伦敦金融城各处，各自行走直到遇见彼此，逐渐聚成一个行进的方阵。
works.idea_en: A decentralised rule for self-assembly: meet, fall into step, keep searching.
works.idea_zh: 一条去中心化的自组织规则：相遇、并步、继续寻找。
works.protocol: Each guard enters the City alone and walks in full ceremonial dress; on meeting another guard they fall into step and search together; when the 8 × 8 square is complete it marches to the nearest bridge, where the guards break step and disperse.
works.protocol_zh: 每名士兵身着礼服独自进入金融城行走；遇到另一名士兵就并步同行、一起寻找；当 8×8 的方阵完整时，方阵走向最近的桥，上桥后士兵们散步、解散。
works.collective: Sixty-four guards carried out the rule early one Sunday morning in July 2004 in the empty Square Mile; the convergence was filmed by Rafael Ortega for Artangel's Seven Walks commission.
works.collective_zh: 2004 年 7 月的一个周日清晨，64 名士兵在空荡荡的金融城执行了这条规则；拉斐尔·奥尔特加为 Artangel 委托的《七次行走》拍下了这次汇合。

works.title: Barrenderos (Sweepers)
works.description: A line of Mexico City street sweepers pushed the rubbish of a street ahead of their brooms, street after street, until the accumulated mass could no longer be moved.
works.description_zh: 一排墨西哥城的街道清洁工用扫帚把街上的垃圾一路向前推，一条街接一条街，直到堆积的垃圾再也推不动。
works.idea_en: A work that ends when the shared load becomes too heavy: the rule contains its own stopping condition.
works.idea_zh: 当共同的负担重到推不动时作品结束：规则自带终止条件。
works.protocol: Sweepers form a line across the street and push everything in front of them forward without removing it; they continue from street to street until the pile stops moving.
works.protocol_zh: 清洁工横跨街道排成一排，把前方的一切向前推而不清走；从一条街推到下一条街，直到垃圾堆停下。
works.collective: Municipal sweepers in the historic centre of Mexico City performed the action, filmed with Julien Devaux; the growing wall of rubbish records their joint effort and its limit.
works.collective_zh: 墨西哥城历史中心的市政清洁工完成了这次行动，由朱利安·德沃拍摄；不断增高的垃圾墙记录了他们的共同努力及其极限。

works.title: The Modern Procession
works.description: On 23 June 2002 a religious-style procession carried replicas of MoMA's icons, and the artist Kiki Smith, from Manhattan across the Queensboro Bridge to the museum's temporary home in Queens.
works.description_zh: 2002 年 6 月 23 日，一支宗教游行式的队伍抬着 MoMA 馆藏名作的复制品和艺术家琪琪·史密斯，从曼哈顿经皇后区大桥走到博物馆在皇后区的临时馆址。
works.idea_en: Moving a museum as a ritual: the collection travels on the shoulders of the public.
works.idea_zh: 把搬迁博物馆变成仪式：藏品由公众扛在肩上迁移。
works.protocol: Participants carry palanquins with replicas of works from the museum's collection, including Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon and Duchamp's Bicycle Wheel, and the artist Kiki Smith as a 'living icon', along a fixed route at the slow pace set by a brass band, from MoMA on 53rd Street to MoMA QNS.
works.protocol_zh: 参与者抬着载有馆藏作品复制品的轿子，包括毕加索的《亚维农少女》和杜尚的《自行车轮》，还有作为“活圣像”的艺术家琪琪·史密斯，按固定路线、随铜管乐队定下的慢速，从 53 街的 MoMA 走到 MoMA QNS。
works.collective: Some one hundred participants walked for about three hours with the Banda de Santa Cecilia, commissioned with the Public Art Fund; the procession marked MoMA's temporary move to Queens.
works.collective_zh: 约一百名参与者随圣塞西莉亚乐队走了约三个小时，由公共艺术基金会联合委托；这次游行标记了 MoMA 暂迁皇后区。

works.title: Bridge/Puente
works.description: Fishermen in Havana and in Key West each formed a line of boats heading out to sea toward the other shore, so that from each coast the line seemed to continue to the horizon as a floating bridge.
works.description_zh: 哈瓦那和基韦斯特的渔民各自排出一列驶向对岸的船队，从两岸望去，船线仿佛一直延伸到海平线，成为一座漂浮的桥。
works.idea_en: Two crowds build one impossible line from opposite sides of a political border.
works.idea_zh: 两群人从政治边界的两侧，共同搭建一条不可能完成的线。
works.protocol: Starting at the water's edge, each boat rows out and anchors a few metres behind the previous one, pointing toward the opposite coast, until the line reaches the horizon; the same rule runs simultaneously on both shores.
works.protocol_zh: 从水边开始，每条船驶出并停泊在前一条船后方几米处，船头指向对岸，直到船线延伸至海平线；两岸同时执行同一条规则。
works.collective: Fishing communities in Cuba and Florida carried out the action in 2006 with Taiyana Pimentel and Cuauhtémoc Medina; it responded to the legal question of whether Cuban migrants caught at sea count as having reached land.
works.collective_zh: 2006 年，古巴和佛罗里达的渔民社群与泰亚娜·皮门特尔和夸乌特莫克·梅迪纳一起完成了这次行动；它回应的是一个法律问题：在海上被截获的古巴移民是否算已登陆。

works.title: Don't Cross the Bridge Before You Get to the River
works.description: On 12 August 2008 a line of children in Tarifa, each carrying a boat made from a shoe, walked into the sea toward Morocco while a second line of children in Tangier walked toward Spain.
works.description_zh: 2008 年 8 月 12 日，塔里法的一列孩子各自拿着用鞋子做的小船走进大海、朝向摩洛哥，而丹吉尔的另一列孩子朝向西班牙走去。
works.idea_en: Children's play as a rule that stitches two continents together on the horizon.
works.idea_zh: 孩子的游戏成为一条规则，在海平线上把两块大陆缝在一起。
works.protocol: On each shore children form a single file and wade out holding shoe-boats; the two lines, one leaving Europe and one leaving Africa, are meant to meet on the horizon.
works.protocol_zh: 两岸的孩子各排成一列，捧着鞋船涉水前行；一列从欧洲出发，一列从非洲出发，两列在海平线上“相遇”。
works.collective: Children from Tarifa and Tangier performed the action, filmed simultaneously on both sides of the Strait of Gibraltar with Fundación Montenmedio Arte.
works.collective_zh: 塔里法和丹吉尔的孩子完成了这次行动，在直布罗陀海峡两岸同时拍摄，合作方为 Montenmedio 艺术基金会。

works.title: Rhythm 0
works.description: For six hours at Studio Morra in Naples, Abramović stood still beside a table of 72 objects, from a rose and honey to scissors, a scalpel and a loaded gun, which the audience could use on her as they wished.
works.description_zh: 在那不勒斯莫拉工作室的六个小时里，阿布拉莫维奇静立在一张摆着 72 件物品的桌旁，从玫瑰、蜂蜜到剪刀、手术刀和一把上膛的枪，观众可以随意用它们作用于她。
works.idea_en: Hand the audience total permission and a fixed set of tools, and the crowd writes the piece.
works.idea_zh: 给观众全部许可和一套固定工具，作品就由人群写成。
works.protocol: Written instruction on the wall: 'There are 72 objects on the table that one can use on me as desired. Performance. I am the object. During this period I take full responsibility.' Duration fixed at six hours (8 pm to 2 am); the artist does not react.
works.protocol_zh: 墙上的书面指令：“桌上有 72 件物品，任何人都可以随意用在我身上。表演。我是客体。在此期间我承担全部责任。”时长固定为六小时（晚 8 点至凌晨 2 点）；艺术家不作任何反应。
works.collective: The audience began gently and grew aggressive: they cut off her clothes, cut her skin and at one point held the loaded gun to her head, until a protective faction intervened. When the six hours ended and she moved toward them, the audience left.
works.collective_zh: 观众一开始很温和，随后变得越来越具攻击性：剪掉她的衣服、划破她的皮肤，一度把上膛的枪抵在她头上，直到另一派观众出面保护。六小时结束、她走向人群时，观众纷纷离开。

works.title: The Artist Is Present
works.description: During her MoMA retrospective (14 March – 31 May 2010) Abramović sat silently at a table in the atrium every day the museum was open, while visitors took turns sitting in the chair opposite for as long as they chose.
works.description_zh: 在 MoMA 回顾展期间（2010 年 3 月 14 日至 5 月 31 日），阿布拉莫维奇在博物馆开放的每一天都静坐在中庭的桌旁，观众轮流坐到她对面，想坐多久就坐多久。
works.idea_en: One chair, one rule (sit and look), and a queue that becomes the public face of the work.
works.idea_zh: 一把椅子、一条规则（坐下并对视），排队的人群成为作品的公共面孔。
works.protocol: One visitor at a time may sit in the empty chair facing the artist, in silence and without touching; each sitter decides how long to stay; the artist remains seated for the museum's full opening hours.
works.protocol_zh: 一次只允许一名观众坐到艺术家对面的空椅上，保持沉默、不得触碰；每人自己决定坐多久；艺术家在博物馆全部开放时间内保持坐姿。
works.collective: Over nearly three months, many hundreds of visitors sat with her, many of them moved to tears, while crowds queued, sometimes overnight; the sitters' faces were photographed and published as part of the work's record.
works.collective_zh: 近三个月里，数以百计的观众与她对坐，不少人落泪，排队的人群有时通宵等候；每位对坐者的面孔都被拍下并作为作品记录发布。

works.title: This Progress
works.description: At the Guggenheim, which Sehgal emptied of all art, visitors walking up Frank Lloyd Wright's ramp were handed from a child to a teenager, a young adult and an older person, each continuing a conversation about progress.
works.description_zh: 赛格尔清空了古根海姆美术馆的全部艺术品，沿弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特螺旋坡道上行的观众，依次由一个孩子、一个少年、一个青年和一位年长者接手，延续一场关于“进步”的对话。
works.idea_en: The artwork is a relay of conversation passed between generations and completed by each visitor.
works.idea_zh: 作品是一场在几代人之间接力的对话，由每位观众补完。
works.protocol: At the base of the ramp a child asks the visitor what progress is; at set points the conversation is handed on to an older interpreter, who picks up and redirects it; no objects, no photography, no written instructions.
works.protocol_zh: 坡道底部，一个孩子问观众什么是进步；在固定位置，对话被交给更年长的诠释者，由他们接过话题并转向；没有物品、不准拍照、没有书面说明。
works.collective: Interpreters of four age groups held a different conversation with every group of visitors over the six-week run; it was the first live work acquired by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
works.collective_zh: 四个年龄层的诠释者在六周展期内与每一组观众进行各不相同的对话；它是所罗门·R·古根海姆美术馆收藏的第一件现场作品。

works.title: These Associations
works.description: For the Unilever Series in Tate Modern's Turbine Hall, a group of about 70 participants walked, ran, sang and gathered in the hall, and broke off to tell individual visitors personal stories.
works.description_zh: 在泰特现代美术馆涡轮大厅的联合利华系列中，约 70 名参与者在大厅里行走、奔跑、歌唱、聚散，并不时离开群体，向个别观众讲述个人故事。
works.idea_en: A crowd choreographed by rules, which dissolves into one-to-one intimacy with strangers.
works.idea_zh: 由规则编排的人群，随时化为与陌生人的一对一亲密交谈。
works.protocol: Participants follow a set of oral rules for group movement (slow walking, running, chasing, choral singing) and, at their own choice, stop a visitor to share a story about belonging, arrival or intimacy; nothing is fixed in writing and photography is refused.
works.protocol_zh: 参与者遵循一套口头传授的集体移动规则（慢走、奔跑、追逐、合唱），并可自行选择拦下一位观众，讲述一个关于归属、抵达或亲密的故事；没有任何书面固定，也拒绝拍照。
works.collective: Around 70 storytellers recruited in London performed in turns during the 2012 run, producing a mass of individual encounters that were never recorded.
works.collective_zh: 约 70 名在伦敦招募的讲述者在 2012 年展期内轮流表演，留下大量从未被记录的个人相遇。

works.title: Touch Sanitation Performance
works.description: Over eleven months in 1979–1980 Ukeles visited all 59 sanitation districts of New York and shook the hand of every sanitation worker, saying to each: 'Thank you for keeping New York City alive.'
works.description_zh: 1979 至 1980 年的十一个月里，尤克里斯走遍纽约全部 59 个环卫区，与每一位环卫工人握手，并对每个人说：“谢谢你让纽约活着。”
works.idea_en: A ritual with a completeness rule: the work is finished only when every member of the workforce has been reached.
works.idea_zh: 一场带有完整性规则的仪式：只有触及整个劳动群体的每一位成员，作品才算完成。
works.protocol: The artist must meet every one of the Department's workers in person, across all shifts and all 59 districts, and perform the same handshake and the same sentence with each.
works.protocol_zh: 艺术家必须在所有班次、全部 59 个区亲自见到环卫局的每一名工人，并对每个人完成同样的握手、说同样的话。
works.collective: About 8,500 sanitation employees took part in the handshake ritual as Ukeles crossed the city ten times; the Department's commissioner later said the performance opened up the humiliation many workers had carried.
works.collective_zh: 尤克里斯十次横穿城市，约 8500 名环卫员工参与了握手仪式；环卫局局长后来说，这次表演揭开了许多工人一直背负的屈辱。
keywords: New York City Department of Sanitation

works.title: I Make Maintenance Art One Hour Every Day
works.description: Ukeles invited the 300 maintenance workers of 55 Water Street, the building housing the Whitney's downtown branch, to declare one hour of their daily shift to be art.
works.description_zh: 尤克里斯邀请水街 55 号（惠特尼美术馆下城分馆所在大楼）的 300 名维护工人，把每天班次中的一个小时宣布为艺术。
works.idea_en: Art by declaration: the same labour, relabelled by its workers for one hour a day.
works.idea_zh: 以宣告成立的艺术：同样的劳动，由工人自己每天改称一小时为艺术。
works.protocol: Each worker designates one hour of the eight-hour shift as maintenance art and wears a button during it; Ukeles photographs every participant with a Polaroid, and the photos are sorted with colour-coded labels on a wall chart.
works.protocol_zh: 每名工人把八小时班次中的一个小时指定为维护艺术，并在这一小时佩戴徽章；尤克里斯用宝丽来为每位参与者拍照，照片按彩色标签归入一面墙上的图表。
works.collective: About 300 workers on day and night shifts took part over six weeks (16 September – 20 October 1976), producing 720 Polaroids; the installation entered the Whitney's collection in 2017.
works.collective_zh: 约 300 名日班和夜班工人在六周内（1976 年 9 月 16 日至 10 月 20 日）参与，产生了 720 张宝丽来照片；这件装置于 2017 年入藏惠特尼美术馆。

works.title: Tatlin's Whisper #6 (Havana Version)
works.description: At the 10th Havana Biennial Bruguera set up a podium and open microphone where anyone could speak uncensored for one minute, while performers in military dress placed a white dove on each speaker's shoulder.
works.description_zh: 在第十届哈瓦那双年展上，布鲁格拉设置了讲台和开放麦克风，任何人都可以不受审查地发言一分钟，身着军装的表演者会在每位发言者肩上放一只白鸽。
works.idea_en: A one-minute rule turns a stage into a temporary zone of free speech.
works.idea_zh: 一分钟的规则把讲台变成一个临时的言论自由区。
works.protocol: Any member of the audience may take the podium and speak for exactly one minute without censorship; two performers in military dress place a white dove on each speaker's shoulder; 200 disposable cameras are handed out to the audience.
works.protocol_zh: 任何观众都可以走上讲台，不受审查地发言整整一分钟；两名身着军装的表演者在每位发言者肩上放一只白鸽；现场向观众发放 200 台一次性相机。
works.collective: On 29 March 2009 at the Centro Wifredo Lam, members of the public, including the blogger Yoani Sánchez, used their minute to call for freedom and democracy; the Cuban authorities denounced the event, and later attempts to restage it in Havana led to Bruguera's arrest.
works.collective_zh: 2009 年 3 月 29 日，在威弗雷多·林中心，包括博主约阿尼·桑切斯在内的公众用自己的一分钟呼吁自由与民主；古巴当局谴责了这一活动，后来在哈瓦那重演的尝试导致布鲁格拉被捕。

works.title: Tatlin's Whisper #5
works.description: Two mounted police officers rode into Tate Modern's Turbine Hall and used crowd-control techniques on the visitors, herding and dispersing them as if managing a protest.
works.description_zh: 两名骑警骑马进入泰特现代美术馆涡轮大厅，用人群管控手段对待观众，像处理抗议人群一样驱赶、驱散他们。
works.idea_en: The audience becomes the material: a crowd experiences, in its own bodies, the rules used to control crowds.
works.idea_zh: 观众成为材料：人群用自己的身体经历用来管控人群的规则。
works.protocol: Real mounted police officers apply standard crowd-control manoeuvres to whoever is in the hall; visitors are not told it is a performance and respond as they choose.
works.protocol_zh: 真正的骑警对大厅里的所有人施行标准的人群管控动作；观众事先不被告知这是表演，由他们自行反应。
works.collective: Tate visitors were pushed, grouped and scattered by the horses; the crowd's compliance and resistance formed the work, which is now in Tate's collection.
works.collective_zh: 泰特的观众被马匹推挤、聚拢和驱散；人群的服从与抵抗构成了作品，它现为泰特馆藏。

works.title: Immigrant Movement International
works.description: A storefront community space in Corona, Queens, run as an artwork and a political movement, offering free classes, legal and health services to immigrant residents.
works.description_zh: 设在纽约皇后区科罗纳的一处临街社区空间，作为艺术作品和政治运动运营，为移民居民提供免费课程以及法律和健康服务。
works.idea_en: Useful art: an institution whose programme is written by the community it serves.
works.idea_zh: 有用的艺术：一个由其服务的社群来编写节目的机构。
works.protocol: The storefront is free and open to residents; workshops and services are offered by residents, artists and partner organisations; the artist lived for a year in a small apartment in Corona with immigrant families while starting the project.
works.protocol_zh: 临街空间免费向居民开放；工作坊和服务由居民、艺术家和合作机构提供；项目启动时，艺术家在科罗纳一间小公寓里与移民家庭同住了一年。
works.collective: Residents, mostly Latin American immigrants, ran workshops on English, immigration law, dance, bicycle repair, screen printing and more from 2011 to 2015, in partnership with the Queens Museum and Creative Time; IMI also joined the Occupy Wall Street marches.
works.collective_zh: 2011 至 2015 年，以拉美移民为主的居民在这里开设英语、移民法律、舞蹈、自行车维修、丝网印刷等工作坊，合作方为皇后区美术馆和 Creative Time；IMI 也加入了“占领华尔街”的游行。

works.title: Fairytale (童话)
works.description: Ai Weiwei brought 1,001 mainland Chinese citizens, chosen through an open call on his blog, to Kassel for documenta 12, and placed 1,001 Qing dynasty chairs throughout the exhibition.
works.description_zh: 艾未未通过博客公开征集，选出 1001 名中国大陆公民带到卡塞尔参加第十二届文献展，并在展场各处放置了 1001 把清代椅子。
works.idea_en: The participants' journey, not an object, is the sculpture.
works.idea_zh: 作品不是物件，而是参与者的旅程。
works.protocol: Anyone in mainland China could apply through the blog by filling in a questionnaire of about 100 questions; the project organised visas, travel and lodging; participants came to Kassel in five groups and were free to act as they wished.
works.protocol_zh: 中国大陆任何人都可以通过博客报名，填写约 100 个问题的问卷；项目统一办理签证、交通和住宿；参与者分五批来到卡塞尔，行动完全自由。
works.collective: More than 3,000 people applied within days; 1,001 travelled in five groups, many leaving China for the first time, and their experiences were recorded in a film and in the questionnaires.
works.collective_zh: 几天之内就有 3000 多人报名；1001 人分五批出行，其中许多人第一次离开中国，他们的经历记录在一部影片和问卷里。

works.title: The Battle of Orgreave
works.description: A re-enactment, on the original site in South Yorkshire, of the 1984 confrontation between striking miners and police at the Orgreave coking plant, performed by historical re-enactment societies together with former miners and police officers.
works.description_zh: 在南约克郡原址重演 1984 年罢工矿工与警察在奥格里夫炼焦厂的冲突，由历史重演协会与当年的矿工和警察共同完成。
works.idea_en: Re-enactment as a protocol for a community to replay and reclaim its own history.
works.idea_zh: 把历史重演当作一种协议，让一个社群重演并重新拥有自己的历史。
works.protocol: The confrontation is restaged on the original site in the sequence reconstructed from witnesses and archives, directed by re-enactment specialist Howard Giles; historical re-enactment societies play alongside former strikers and police who were there in 1984.
works.protocol_zh: 在原址按照根据目击者和档案重建的顺序重演这场冲突，由历史重演专家霍华德·贾尔斯指挥；历史重演协会成员与 1984 年亲历现场的罢工者和警察一同演出。
works.collective: More than 800 participants, including former miners and police from the original events, restaged the battle in 2001; Mike Figgis filmed it for Artangel and Channel 4 (broadcast 20 October 2002), and the archive entered Tate's collection.
works.collective_zh: 2001 年，800 多名参与者（包括当年事件中的矿工和警察）重演了这场冲突；迈克·菲吉斯为 Artangel 和第四频道拍摄了影片（2002 年 10 月 20 日播出），相关档案入藏泰特。

works.title: we're here because we're here
works.description: On 1 July 2016, the centenary of the first day of the Somme, about 1,400 volunteers in First World War uniform appeared unannounced in stations, streets and shopping centres across the UK.
works.description_zh: 2016 年 7 月 1 日，索姆河战役首日一百周年，约 1400 名身着一战军装的志愿者未经预告出现在英国各地的车站、街道和商场。
works.idea_en: A silent rule plus a card turns a crowd of volunteers into a nationwide, distributed memorial.
works.idea_zh: 一条沉默的规则加一张卡片，让一群志愿者成为遍布全国的分布式纪念碑。
works.protocol: Each volunteer represents one named soldier killed on 1 July 1916; they do not speak; when approached they hand over a card with that soldier's name, age and regiment and the hashtag #wearehere; at intervals they sing 'We're here because we're here'.
works.protocol_zh: 每名志愿者代表一名 1916 年 7 月 1 日阵亡、有名有姓的士兵；他们不说话；有人走近时递上一张写有该士兵姓名、年龄、所属部队和 #wearehere 标签的卡片；每隔一段时间唱起“我们在这里因为我们在这里”。
works.collective: Around 1,400 volunteers took part in locations across the UK, and members of the public shared their encounters online under #wearehere. It was commissioned by 14-18 NOW and made with Rufus Norris of the National Theatre.
works.collective_zh: 约 1400 名志愿者在英国各地参与，公众在网上以 #wearehere 分享自己的相遇。作品由 14-18 NOW 委托，与国家剧院的鲁弗斯·诺里斯合作完成。

works.title: Signs that say what you want them to say and not Signs that say what someone else wants you to say
works.description: Wearing stopped strangers in London streets, asked each to write whatever they were thinking on a sheet of white card, and photographed them holding it.
works.description_zh: 韦英在伦敦街头拦下陌生人，请他们在一张白卡纸上写下此刻所想，再拍下他们手持卡纸的照片。
works.idea_en: Give the subject the caption, and the portrait becomes a self-authored statement.
works.idea_zh: 把图注交给被拍摄者，肖像就变成本人写下的声明。
works.protocol: Any passer-by who agrees writes their own message on a blank card, without suggestions from the artist, and is photographed holding it; each photo is titled with the words on the card.
works.protocol_zh: 任何同意参与的路人都在空白卡片上写下自己的话，艺术家不作提示，然后手持卡片拍照；每张照片都以卡片上的文字命名。
works.collective: Hundreds of strangers took part in 1992–93, writing confessions and slogans such as 'I'M DESPERATE'; their words, not the artist's, became the titles and content of the series.
works.collective_zh: 1992 至 1993 年，数百名陌生人参与，写下诸如“我很绝望”这样的告白和口号；是他们的话语而非艺术家的话语，成为这一系列的标题和内容。

works.title: untitled 1992 (free)
works.description: At 303 Gallery in New York Tiravanija moved the contents of the gallery office into the exhibition space and turned the office into a kitchen where he cooked Thai curry and served it free to anyone who came.
works.description_zh: 在纽约 303 画廊，提拉瓦尼把画廊办公室的物品搬进展厅，把办公室改成厨房，烹制泰式咖喱，免费招待任何来访者。
works.idea_en: A standing offer (free food, open door) whose social consequences are the artwork.
works.idea_zh: 一个长期有效的邀请（免费食物、敞开的门），它引发的社交后果就是作品。
works.protocol: The gallery's back office is exposed and its kitchen runs during opening hours; curry and rice are cooked daily and given free to every visitor; in MoMA's collection the work can be re-activated with food prepared in the museum's kitchen and served daily.
works.protocol_zh: 画廊后台办公区完全敞开，厨房在开放时间运作；每天煮咖喱和米饭，免费分给每位观众；在 MoMA 的收藏中，这件作品可以用博物馆厨房每天制作的食物重新激活。
works.collective: Visitors ate, talked and lingered, turning the gallery into a canteen; the work was re-staged at David Zwirner (2007) and at MoMA (2011), where a free vegetarian curry lunch was served every day.
works.collective_zh: 观众在这里吃饭、交谈、逗留，把画廊变成食堂；作品后来在大卫·卓纳画廊（2007）和 MoMA（2011）重演，MoMA 每天免费供应素咖喱午餐。

works.title: Baba Antropofágica (Anthropophagic Drool)
works.description: A group kneels around one person lying on the floor; each has a spool of coloured thread in the mouth and pulls out the saliva-soaked thread onto the body below until it is covered in a web.
works.description_zh: 一群人跪在一名躺在地上的人周围；每人嘴里含一卷彩色线，把被唾液浸湿的线一点点拉出、铺在下方的身体上，直到身体被一张网覆盖。
works.idea_en: A collective body produced by a simple bodily instruction shared by the group.
works.idea_zh: 一条由全体共享的简单身体指令，造出一个集体的身体。
works.protocol: One volunteer lies on the floor; the others kneel around, take thread spools into their mouths and unwind the saliva-soaked thread onto the volunteer; when the spools are empty the group lifts the web off together.
works.protocol_zh: 一名志愿者躺在地上；其他人跪在四周，把线轴含进嘴里，把被唾液浸湿的线拉出铺到志愿者身上；线轴用完后，全体一起把这张网揭下。
works.collective: Clark devised it with her students at the Sorbonne in Paris, where she taught from 1972; it has been re-enacted by groups in museums and workshops, and each performance produces a different web.
works.collective_zh: 克拉克与她自 1972 年起在巴黎索邦大学教授的学生一起创作了这件作品；此后在美术馆和工作坊中被不同群体重演，每次都织出不同的网。

works.title: Caminhando (Walking)
works.description: An instruction anyone can carry out: make a Möbius strip from paper and cut along its length with scissors, choosing a new path each time around, until the strip is too narrow to cut.
works.description_zh: 一条任何人都能执行的指令：用纸做一条莫比乌斯环，用剪刀沿长度方向剪下去，每一圈都选择一条新路径，直到纸条窄到无法再剪。
works.idea_en: The artwork moves from object to act: it exists only while someone is doing it.
works.idea_zh: 作品从物件转为行为：只有有人在做的时候它才存在。
works.protocol: Take a strip of paper, twist it once and glue the ends into a Möbius strip; pierce it and cut continuously along its length without crossing an earlier cut; the work ends when no path is left.
works.protocol_zh: 取一条纸，扭转一次、把两端粘成莫比乌斯环；在纸上戳一个口，沿长度方向连续剪，不得与之前的剪口相交；无路可剪时作品结束。
works.collective: Clark published the proposition so that viewers could make it themselves; it has since been performed by museum visitors and in workshops worldwide, including at MoMA's 2014 retrospective.
works.collective_zh: 克拉克把这个提议公开，让观众自己去做；此后世界各地的美术馆观众和工作坊参与者都执行过它，包括 MoMA 2014 年的回顾展。

works.title: Parangolés
works.description: Capes, banners and tents of layered fabric, plastic and matting that are completed only when a person wears them and dances; Oiticica made them with dancers from the Mangueira samba school.
works.description_zh: 由多层布料、塑料和草席做成的斗篷、旗帜和帐篷，只有当人穿上并舞动时才算完成；奥迪塞卡与芒格拉桑巴学校的舞者一起创作了它们。
works.idea_en: Sculpture that needs a wearer: the viewer becomes the moving support of the work.
works.idea_zh: 需要穿戴者的雕塑：观众成为作品移动的支撑。
works.protocol: A Parangolé is not displayed on a stand but handed to a participant, who puts it on and moves; the unfolding of colour and text depends on the wearer's dance.
works.protocol_zh: 《帕兰戈莱》不放在展台上展示，而是交给参与者，由其穿上并移动；色彩与文字如何展开取决于穿戴者的舞蹈。
works.collective: At the opening of Opinião 65 at the Museum of Modern Art of Rio de Janeiro in 1965, Oiticica's friends from Mangueira arrived to dance in the capes and were refused entry; they danced outside with the public, and the capes have since been worn by visitors in exhibitions.
works.collective_zh: 1965 年里约热内卢现代艺术博物馆“意见 65”展开幕时，奥迪塞卡在芒格拉的朋友前来穿着斗篷跳舞却被拒之门外；他们在馆外与公众一起跳舞，此后展览中的观众也常穿上这些斗篷。

works.title: Théorie de la dérive (Theory of the Dérive)
works.description: Debord's text sets out the dérive: small groups drifting rapidly through a city, letting its atmospheres, rather than errands, decide their path, and comparing notes afterwards.
works.description_zh: 德波的文章阐述了“漂移”：小组在城市中快速穿行，让城市的氛围而不是日常事务决定路线，事后再比对各自的观察。
works.idea_en: A walking protocol for groups that turns a city into a field of experiment.
works.idea_zh: 一套给群体的行走协议，把城市变成实验场。
works.protocol: Drift in several small groups of two or three people who share the same awareness; groups change composition between dérives; beyond about ten people the dérive splits; the average duration is one day, between two periods of sleep; impressions are cross-checked between groups.
works.protocol_zh: 分成几个两三人的小组漂移，组员具有相同的意识水平；每次漂移之间更换组员；超过十人左右漂移就会分裂；平均时长为一天，即两段睡眠之间；各组之间交叉核对印象。
works.collective: Letterists and Situationists practised dérives in Paris in the 1950s and mapped them in psychogeographic guides such as The Naked City (1957); the text, published in Les Lèvres nues no. 9 (1956) and reprinted in Internationale situationniste no. 2 (1958), is still used by artists and walking groups.
works.collective_zh: 1950 年代，字母主义者和情境主义者在巴黎实践漂移，并在《裸城》（1957）等心理地理指南中绘出路线；这篇文章发表于《裸唇》第 9 期（1956），再刊于《情境主义国际》第 2 期（1958），至今仍被艺术家和行走团体使用。

paper.title: Theory of the Dérive
paper.venue: Les Lèvres nues no. 9 (1956); Internationale situationniste no. 2 (1958)

works.title: Le Jeu de la Guerre (The Game of War / Kriegspiel)
works.description: A two-player strategy game on a board of 25 by 20 squares, modelled on Clausewitzian warfare, in which armies must stay connected to their arsenals through lines of communication.
works.description_zh: 一款双人战略游戏，棋盘为 25×20 格，以克劳塞维茨式战争为模型，军队必须通过交通线与自己的兵工厂保持连接。
works.idea_en: A rule set about supply lines: units that lose contact with their network cannot act.
works.idea_zh: 一套关于补给线的规则：与网络失去联系的单位就无法行动。
works.protocol: Each side has arsenals, forts, infantry, cavalry, artillery and relay units; lines of communication radiate from arsenals and relays; a unit cut off from them is paralysed; each turn allows up to five moves and one attack.
works.protocol_zh: 双方各有兵工厂、堡垒、步兵、骑兵、炮兵和通讯单位；交通线从兵工厂和通讯单位辐射出去；被切断联系的单位陷入瘫痪；每回合最多移动五个单位、发动一次进攻。
works.collective: Debord conceived the game in the 1950s and patented it in 1965; in 1977 he and Gérard Lebovici published the rules in French and English and had a few copies of the board made; in 1987 he and Alice Becker-Ho published a record of a complete game, and the Radical Software Group later released a computer version for online play.
works.collective_zh: 德波在 1950 年代构思了这款游戏，1965 年申请专利；1977 年他与热拉尔·勒博维奇以法英双语出版规则，并制作了少量棋盘；1987 年他与爱丽丝·贝克-何出版了一整局对弈的记录；激进软件小组后来发布了可在线对弈的电脑版本。

works.title: The Crystal Quilt
works.description: On Mother's Day, 10 May 1987, 430 Minnesota women over 60 sat at tables arranged as a quilt in the Crystal Court of Minneapolis's IDS Center and talked about ageing, while their hand movements changed the quilt's pattern.
works.description_zh: 1987 年母亲节（5 月 10 日），430 名 60 岁以上的明尼苏达女性坐在明尼阿波利斯 IDS 中心水晶庭中排成被面图案的桌旁，谈论衰老，她们的手部动作不断改变被面的图案。
works.idea_en: A choreographic score for hands turns a public conversation into a changing image seen from above.
works.idea_zh: 一份写给双手的编舞乐谱，把公共对话变成从上方俯看、不断变化的图像。
works.protocol: Women sit at tables on a quilt-patterned floor designed by Miriam Schapiro and talk about their lives and the place of older women in society; every ten minutes a loon cry or thunderclap signals them to change the position of their hands, changing the pattern seen from above.
works.protocol_zh: 女性坐在米里亚姆·夏皮罗设计的被面图案地面上的桌旁，谈论自己的生活以及年长女性在社会中的位置；每隔十分钟，一声潜鸟叫或雷声提示她们改变双手的位置，从上方看去图案随之改变。
works.collective: 430 women took part, the culmination of the multi-year Whisper Minnesota project with workshops across the state; the performance was broadcast live on PBS and is now in Tate's collection.
works.collective_zh: 430 名女性参与了表演，这是持续数年、在全州开展工作坊的“低语明尼苏达”项目的高潮；表演在 PBS 现场直播，现为泰特馆藏。

works.title: Gramsci Monument
works.description: A plywood and tape structure built and run with residents of Forest Houses, a public housing estate in the Bronx, containing a library, theatre, bar, radio station and daily newspaper dedicated to Antonio Gramsci.
works.description_zh: 与布朗克斯公共住宅区 Forest Houses 的居民一起搭建和运营的胶合板加胶带结构，内有图书馆、剧场、酒吧、电台和日报，献给安东尼奥·葛兰西。
works.idea_en: A monument that exists as paid work, daily programme and shared use for a fixed period.
works.idea_zh: 一座以有偿工作、每日节目和共同使用的方式、在固定期限内存在的纪念碑。
works.protocol: The monument must be sited in a housing estate with residents' agreement; residents are paid to build and staff it; it is open every day with a fixed programme (lectures, workshops, newspaper, radio) and is dismantled after the set period.
works.protocol_zh: 纪念碑必须在征得居民同意的公共住宅区内建造；居民受雇建造和值守；每天开放，有固定节目（讲座、工作坊、报纸、电台），到期即拆除。
works.collective: More than 40 Forest Houses residents were hired, 15 of them to build the structure; from 1 July to 15 September 2013 residents and visitors used it daily for lectures by Marcus Steinweg, children's workshops, radio shows and a newspaper; it was commissioned by Dia Art Foundation.
works.collective_zh: Forest Houses 雇用了 40 多名居民，其中 15 人参与建造；2013 年 7 月 1 日至 9 月 15 日，居民和访客每天在这里听马库斯·施泰因韦格的讲座、参加儿童工作坊、做电台节目和编报纸；作品由迪亚艺术基金会委托。

works.title: The Moving Garden
works.description: A long granite table in the gallery holds hundreds of fresh flowers; visitors may take one on two conditions about what they do with it after leaving the museum.
works.description_zh: 展厅里一张长长的花岗岩桌上插着数百枝鲜花；观众可以带走一枝，但离开美术馆后必须满足两个条件。
works.idea_en: A gift with conditions: the museum's content is released into the city through strangers.
works.idea_zh: 附带条件的礼物：美术馆的内容经由陌生人流入城市。
works.protocol: Take one flower; on leaving the museum, make a detour from your intended route; give the flower to a stranger you feel would benefit from an unexpected act of kindness.
works.protocol_zh: 带走一枝花；离开美术馆时偏离原本的路线绕一段路；把花送给一位你觉得需要一次意外善意的陌生人。
works.collective: First shown at the 10th Biennale de Lyon in 2009 and restaged at the Brooklyn Museum, the NGV and elsewhere, the work has been carried out by visitors handing flowers to strangers in each host city; the result exists only as these unrecorded exchanges.
works.collective_zh: 作品首展于 2009 年第十届里昂双年展，之后在布鲁克林博物馆、维多利亚国立美术馆等地重演，每座城市的观众都把花送给了陌生人；结果只以这些未被记录的交换存在。

works.title: Appearance (Poiavlenie) and Trips Out of Town
works.description: In the first action of Collective Actions, invited spectators waited in a snowy field in Izmailovsky Park until two organisers emerged from the woods, crossed the field and handed them certificates of presence.
works.description_zh: 在“集体行动”小组的第一次行动中，受邀观众在伊兹梅洛沃公园的雪地里等待，直到两名组织者从树林中走出、穿过田野，向他们发放在场证明。
works.idea_en: The audience's waiting and attention are the event; a signed document certifies that they took part.
works.idea_zh: 观众的等待和注意力就是事件；一份签名文件证明他们参与其中。
works.protocol: Viewers are invited in advance to travel to an empty field outside the city at a set time, without knowing what will happen; minimal events take place at the edge of perception; participants receive or sign documents and later write accounts that are collected in the 'Trips Out of Town' volumes.
works.protocol_zh: 观众事先受邀在约定时间前往城外的空旷田野，不知道会发生什么；极少量的事件在感知的边缘发生；参与者领取或签署文件，之后写下讲述，收入《出城之旅》文集。
works.collective: About thirty people attended Appearance on 13 March 1976; the group went on to stage many more actions over the following decades for a regular circle of viewer-participants, whose narratives fill the samizdat volumes of Trips Out of Town.
works.collective_zh: 1976 年 3 月 13 日约有三十人参加了《出现》；此后几十年，小组为一批固定的观众兼参与者组织了许多次行动，他们的讲述构成了地下出版物《出城之旅》的主体。

works.title: MoMA Poll
works.description: In MoMA's Information exhibition, visitors answered a political question about Governor Nelson Rockefeller, a MoMA trustee, by dropping ballots into one of two transparent boxes.
works.description_zh: 在 MoMA 的“信息”展中，观众通过把选票投入两个透明箱子之一，回答一个关于纳尔逊·洛克菲勒州长（也是 MoMA 理事）的政治问题。
works.idea_en: A live poll in which the museum's own audience produces the evidence, visible as it accumulates.
works.idea_zh: 一次现场投票，由美术馆自己的观众产生证据，并随累积而清晰可见。
works.protocol: Question on the wall: 'Would the fact that Governor Rockefeller has not denounced President Nixon's Indochina policy be a reason for your not voting for him in November?' Each visitor may drop a ballot in the YES or the NO box; the transparent boxes keep the running count visible.
works.protocol_zh: 墙上的问题：“洛克菲勒州长没有谴责尼克松总统的印度支那政策，这一事实会不会成为你十一月不投票给他的理由？”每位观众可以把选票投进“是”或“否”的箱子；透明的票箱让累计结果始终可见。
works.collective: Visitors voted throughout the exhibition; by the end there were roughly twice as many Yes ballots as No ballots, a public verdict gathered inside an institution Rockefeller helped run.
works.collective_zh: 观众在整个展期内投票；展览结束时，“是”的选票约为“否”的两倍，这是在洛克菲勒参与管理的机构内部收集到的公开裁决。

works.title: Key to the City
works.description: At a booth in Times Square, members of the public awarded each other a 'key to the city' in a one-to-one ceremony; the key opened locks at more than 20 sites across New York's five boroughs.
works.description_zh: 在时代广场的一个授钥亭里，公众在一对一的仪式中互相授予“城市之钥”；这把钥匙能打开纽约五个区 20 多个地点的锁。
works.idea_en: A civic honour made peer-to-peer: anyone can bestow it, and it actually opens doors.
works.idea_zh: 把公民荣誉变成点对点：任何人都能授予，而且它真的能开门。
works.protocol: You cannot take a key for yourself: one person must give it to another in a short ceremony at the booth; the key then opens the gates, doors and lockers of the participating sites for the duration of the project.
works.protocol_zh: 不能给自己拿钥匙：必须由一个人在授钥亭的简短仪式中把钥匙交给另一个人；在项目期间，这把钥匙可以打开各参与地点的大门、房门和柜子。
works.collective: In June 2010 thousands of keys were exchanged in one-to-one ceremonies; recipients then used them to explore community gardens, cemeteries, museums and back doors across the city. Presented by Creative Time with the City of New York.
works.collective_zh: 2010 年 6 月，数以千计的钥匙在一对一的仪式中被授出；获赠者随后用它们探访全市的社区花园、墓地、博物馆和后门。由 Creative Time 与纽约市政府联合呈现。

works.title: The Act of Drinking Beer with Friends Is the Highest Form of Art
works.description: Marioni invited friends to drink beer with him at the Oakland Museum and declared the gathering the artwork; it has continued as a weekly salon in San Francisco for decades.
works.description_zh: 马里奥尼邀请朋友在奥克兰博物馆和他一起喝啤酒，并宣布这场聚会就是艺术作品；此后几十年，它作为每周一次的沙龙在旧金山延续。
works.idea_en: A recurring social ritual declared as art; its residue (bottles, debris) is the only object.
works.idea_zh: 被宣布为艺术的定期社交仪式；它的残留物（酒瓶、杂物）是唯一的实物。
works.protocol: The artist invites friends to drink beer and talk at a set time and place; nothing else is required; the empty bottles and debris are left in place and can be exhibited.
works.protocol_zh: 艺术家邀请朋友在约定的时间和地点喝啤酒、聊天；除此之外没有任何要求；空瓶和杂物原地保留，可以展出。
works.collective: Sixteen friends attended the first event at the Oakland Museum in 1970; by 1973 the gatherings had become weekly salons, held on Wednesdays for decades; SFMOMA showed and acquired the debris installation FREE BEER in 1979.
works.collective_zh: 1970 年奥克兰博物馆的首次活动有 16 位朋友参加；到 1973 年聚会变成每周一次的沙龙，此后几十年都在周三举行；旧金山现代艺术博物馆于 1979 年展出并收藏了由残留物构成的装置《免费啤酒》。

works.title: TAPP und TASTKINO (Tap and Touch Cinema)
works.description: EXPORT strapped a small box with a curtain over her naked chest and walked through city streets while Peter Weibel invited passers-by through a megaphone to reach into this 'cinema' and touch her.
works.description_zh: 艾丝波尔把一个带帘子的小盒子绑在裸露的胸前走上街头，彼得·魏贝尔用扩音器邀请路人把手伸进这座“电影院”触摸她。
works.idea_en: Expanded cinema as a public rule: the audience must decide, face to face, whether to 'watch'.
works.idea_zh: 作为公共规则的扩展电影：观众必须面对面地决定要不要“观看”。
works.protocol: The box is the screen; anyone who accepts the invitation may reach through the curtain and touch; the 'screening' is short and then passes to the next viewer, in public and in full view of the crowd.
works.protocol_zh: 盒子就是银幕；任何接受邀请的人都可以把手伸进帘子触摸；每场“放映”都很短，随后轮到下一位观众，全程在公共场合、在人群注视下进行。
works.collective: Passers-by in several European cities between 1968 and 1971 either took up or refused the invitation; their hesitation, embarrassment and choices became the content of the piece.
works.collective_zh: 1968 至 1971 年间，欧洲多个城市的路人或接受、或拒绝了邀请；他们的犹豫、尴尬与选择成为作品的内容。

works.title: Frozen Grand Central
works.description: On 26 January 2008, 207 volunteers froze in place at the same moment in the main concourse of Grand Central Terminal and held still for five minutes among commuters.
works.description_zh: 2008 年 1 月 26 日，207 名志愿者在纽约中央车站大厅同一时刻定格，在通勤人群中静止五分钟。
works.idea_en: One synchronised instruction, sent to a volunteer crowd, creates a public anomaly that strangers must interpret.
works.idea_zh: 发给一群志愿者的一条同步指令，制造出陌生人必须自行解读的公共异象。
works.protocol: Volunteers recruited online gather nearby, synchronise watches, drift into the concourse, freeze in whatever pose they are in at the signal, stay frozen for five minutes and then resume as if nothing happened.
works.protocol_zh: 网上招募的志愿者在附近集合、对表，分散进入大厅，信号一到就以当时的姿势定格，保持五分钟，然后若无其事地继续走动。
works.collective: 207 'agents' took part; the video of commuters' reactions became one of the most-watched early YouTube videos, and according to Charlie Todd the prank has been recreated by fans in about 100 cities.
works.collective_zh: 207 名“特工”参与；记录通勤者反应的视频成为早期 YouTube 上观看次数最多的视频之一，据查理·托德说，这一恶作剧已被粉丝在约 100 座城市重演。

leads.name: Joseph Beuys, Honigpumpe am Arbeitsplatz / Free International University (documenta 6, 1977)
leads.why: 100 days of workshops run by different groups around a honey-pump circuit; check whether the workshop format counts as a group protocol.

leads.name: Bill Wasik, The MOB Project (2003)
leads.why: First flash mobs, organised by anonymous email instructions to a crowd; belongs to network/crowdsourced.

leads.name: Yoko Ono, Cut Piece (1964)
leads.why: Audience members cut the performer's clothes one by one; a close relative of Rhythm 0 (likely in the score batch).

leads.name: Mieko Shiomi, Spatial Poem (1965–75)
leads.why: Event instructions mailed to participants worldwide; responses mapped and published. Score or correspondence.

leads.name: Suzanne Lacy, Whisper, the Waves, the Wind (1984) and Between the Door and the Street (2013)
leads.why: Further large choreographed conversations with women; same protocol family as The Crystal Quilt.

leads.name: Jeremy Deller, Procession (Manchester, 2009)
leads.why: Parade made of groups who each chose how to represent themselves.

leads.name: Tania Bruguera, Association of Arte Útil / Hannah Arendt International Institute for Artivism (INSTAR)
leads.why: Institutions run as artworks; check rules and participation.

leads.name: Marina Abramović, Abramović Method (2012–)
leads.why: Instructions and exercises for audiences in groups; check if the group behaviour is the work.

leads.name: Lee Mingwei, The Dining Project / Sonic Blossom / The Mending Project
leads.why: Other gift-and-condition works where strangers carry out the protocol.

leads.name: Hans Haacke, Gallery-Goers' Birthplace and Residence Profile (1969)
leads.why: Visitors mark where they live on maps; audience produces the work's data.

leads.name: Stephen Willats, West London Social Resource Project (1972)
leads.why: Questionnaires and feedback loops with residents; systems-based participatory art.

leads.name: Spencer Tunick, mass nude installations (1992–)
leads.why: Thousands of volunteers follow posing instructions; borderline because the photograph is authored by one person.

leads.name: Hélio Oiticica, Tropicália (1967) and Éden (1969)
leads.why: Environments completed by visitors' behaviour; check whether a rule set exists.

leads.name: Theaster Gates, Dorchester Projects / Rick Lowe, Project Row Houses
leads.why: Social-practice institutions built with neighbourhoods; check whether the rules are authored and addressed to the group.

leads.name: Marinella Senatore, The School of Narrative Dance
leads.why: Nomadic school and parades produced by local participants under a method.

leads.name: Francis Alÿs, Children's Games (1999–)
leads.why: Films existing children's games; the rules are not authored by the artist.

leads.name: Ai Weiwei, Sunflower Seeds (2010)
leads.why: Made by about 1,600 artisans as fabrication labour; no rule shapes a group's behaviour as the work.

leads.name: Lygia Clark, Estruturação do Self (Structuring of the Self, 1976–1988)
leads.why: One-to-one therapeutic sessions with relational objects; not addressed to a group.

leads.name: Christo and Jeanne-Claude, large installations
leads.why: Large paid crews install a design; crowd behaviour is not the work.
